claim: The period T of a simple pendulum in the small-angle limit is given by T = 2π√(L/g), where L is the length of the pendulum and g is the acceleration due to gravity.
The Lyapunov exponent λ of the logistic map f(x) = 4x(1-x) is positive, indicating deterministic chaos.
For a circular orbit under an inverse-square central force F = -k/r^2, the square of the orbital period T is proportional to the cube of the orbital radius a, i.e., T^2 ∝ a^3.

The Lyapunov exponent λ for the logistic map f(x) = 4x(1-x) at r=4 is exactly ln(2), derived from the limit definition λ = lim_{N→∞} (1/N) Σ_{n=0}^{N-1} ln|f'(x_n)|, where x_n is the trajectory starting from x_0 in (0,1).

The error in the numerically computed bifurcation point r_n of the logistic map scales as |r_n - r_c| ∝ δr / |λ_c| where δr is the step size in parameter space and λ_c is the critical eigenvalue at the bifurcation point
